_comment: TEMPLATE — copy this file to `.ruitk-local.json` (gitignored) and fill in what is true for THIS
machine. Every key is OPTIONAL: discovery must succeed with no file present, so add a key only
when the probe can't find a tool or finds the wrong one. Backslashes are doubled, as JSON wants.
Resolution chain (authoritative copy: CLAUDE.md's "Machine-local paths" section):
$ENV_VAR  ->  .ruitk-local.json  ->  PATH + the standard install roots  ->  an error naming all three.
Repo locations are NEVER listed here. They are DERIVED — ${workspaceFolder} in .vscode/**, a
script's own '..', `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` in a skill, `git worktree list` for worktrees.
A written-down repo path breaks every clone whose folder name differs, which is exactly how this
repo's F5 broke when a rename sweep rewrote the folder segment inside a hardcoded launch argument.
`node scripts/check-machine-paths.mjs` is the gate that keeps machine paths out of tracked files.
_engineRoot: Unreal Engine install to build/test against, e.g. "C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.6".
Order: $UE_ROOT wins, then this key, then every Launcher install under the Epic Games root
(scripts/package-plugin.ps1 enumerates them). Set it only to pin one install or to point at an
engine outside the Launcher root. 5.6 is the floor.
_clangFormat: clang-format 19.1.5 — the pinned version; another one reflows Source/ and fails the CI check.
Probed on PATH first, then this key, then the VS 2022 bundle at
<VS install>\VC\Tools\Llvm\x64\bin\clang-format.exe. Set it when neither probe finds it.
